text:
Since 2007, electricity prices in South Africa have gone up by about 900%. Over the same time, prices in general went up by about 150%. Nomsa (an illustration) spends the same R500 on her prepaid meter every month, but each July she gets fewer units. So how did Eskom end up so deep in debt that the government stepped in with up to R254 billion?

Full guide: "How Eskom Went Broke, and What It Costs You Every Month (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.

Sources
- Electricity Minister Kgosientsho Ramokgopa, 18 Aug 2026 (prices since 2007)
- Eskom Debt Relief Act, 2023 (up to R254 billion over three years)
